domain.name: Unreal Engine Production
domain.description: Advanced Unreal production covering Blueprint/C++ boundaries, gameplay framework architecture, large-world systems, PCG, Niagara, Control Rig, Sequencer, performance, memory, and packaging diagnostics. Version-sensitive engine details belong in Current Intelligence.

competencies.name: Blueprint & C++ System Boundaries
competencies.description: Choose where gameplay logic, data, extensibility, and performance-critical behavior should live across Blueprint and C++.
competencies.purpose: Keep systems editable without turning either layer into an unmaintainable bottleneck.

units.title: Blueprint and C++ are complementary layers
units.content: C++ is useful for stable core systems and performance-sensitive abstractions; Blueprint is powerful for composition, tuning, prototyping, and content-facing logic when contracts stay clear.

units.title: Boundary design workflow
units.content: Define system responsibility, identify data and extension points, put stable reusable core logic behind narrow interfaces, expose only needed variables and events, test Blueprint subclasses, and profile before moving logic solely for speed.

units.title: Boundary failure modes
units.content: Avoid giant Blueprints with hidden dependencies, C++ that overexposes internals, Blueprint logic tied to editor-only assumptions, and rewriting working systems without measured need.

drills.title: Design a Blueprint/C++ gameplay boundary
drills.prompt: Split a reusable interaction and inventory system between C++ core logic and Blueprint-facing content logic.

competencies.name: Gameplay Framework Architecture
competencies.description: Use GameMode, GameState, PlayerController, Pawn/Character, components, subsystems, interfaces, and data assets with explicit ownership.
competencies.purpose: Build runtime systems that survive map changes, multiplayer assumptions, and feature growth.

units.title: Framework classes encode lifetime and authority
units.content: Choosing the wrong owner for persistent state, player-specific state, world rules, or services creates lifecycle bugs that surface later.

units.title: Framework ownership workflow
units.content: Classify each state by authority and lifetime, choose the narrowest valid owner, separate presentation from rules, define initialization order, and test travel/restart/respawn behavior.

units.title: Framework failure modes
units.content: Avoid storing persistent data on short-lived Actors, using GameMode for client-visible assumptions, duplicating subsystem responsibilities, and relying on BeginPlay order accidentally.

drills.title: Map a gameplay system onto Unreal framework classes
drills.prompt: Assign ownership for session rules, player profile, spawn state, UI state, inventory, and world services.

competencies.name: World Partition, Data Layers & PCG
competencies.description: Structure large environments with streaming cells, data layers, procedural generation, HLOD, and content ownership.
competencies.purpose: Scale large worlds without loading or editing everything at once.

units.title: Large-world systems are content-lifetime systems
units.content: Streaming, HLOD, data layers, and PCG determine what exists, when it loads, how it is edited, and what can be regenerated safely.

units.title: Large-world workflow
units.content: Define world grid and origin assumptions, classify persistent versus streamed content, use data layers for intentional variants or worksets, keep procedural sources authoritative, validate HLOD and runtime streaming on target hardware.

units.title: Large-world failure modes
units.content: Avoid manually editing generated output without ownership rules, putting critical global systems in streamed cells, creating data-layer combinations no one can reason about, and tuning HLOD only by appearance without memory tests.

drills.title: Design a streamed city district
drills.prompt: Plan World Partition, data layers, HLOD, and PCG ownership for a dense urban environment.

competencies.name: Advanced Materials & Niagara Systems
competencies.description: Build parameterized materials and Niagara effects with reusable modules, data interfaces, and bounded cost.
competencies.purpose: Create sophisticated realtime visuals without losing performance control.

units.title: Realtime effects multiply across screen, particles, and emitters
units.content: Material instructions, overdraw, translucency, lights, particles, collisions, and simulation stages combine into total effect cost.

units.title: Effect-development workflow
units.content: Define visual requirement, build a cheap baseline, expose limited parameters, reuse modules, profile overdraw and simulation cost, test worst-case spawn counts, and create lower-cost scalability variants.

units.title: VFX failure modes
units.content: Avoid uncontrolled translucent layers, per-particle expensive logic by default, dynamic lights on every effect, unbounded spawn rates, and judging cost from one quiet test scene.

drills.title: Design a scalable weather effect
drills.prompt: Build a production plan for rain, splashes, mist, and wet-surface response across scalability levels.

competencies.name: Control Rig & Advanced Animation Pipeline
competencies.description: Use Control Rig, IK, retargeting, additive layers, curves, and runtime animation systems coherently.
competencies.purpose: Create flexible character animation while protecting skeleton and deformation contracts.

units.title: Animation pipeline stages need explicit ownership
units.content: Imported animation, retargeting, Control Rig edits, runtime IK, montages, and procedural layers can conflict if multiple stages write the same transforms without policy.

units.title: Animation integration workflow
units.content: Validate skeleton and retarget pose, establish root-motion policy, define Control Rig edit layer, isolate runtime IK or procedural adjustments, test extreme poses, and verify final runtime blending.

units.title: Animation pipeline failures
units.content: Avoid silently changing skeleton hierarchy, stacking multiple untracked pose corrections, retargeting without pose validation, and baking away editability before the motion is approved.

drills.title: Audit a retargeted character pipeline
drills.prompt: Plan fixes for a character with foot sliding, shoulder distortion, and inconsistent root motion after retargeting.

competencies.name: Sequencer & Virtual Production Workflow
competencies.description: Build complex cinematic timelines with shots, cameras, tracks, sub-sequences, animation, audio, and render handoff.
competencies.purpose: Keep cinematic work editable, reviewable, and render-safe.

units.title: Sequencer is an orchestration layer
units.content: Shots, cameras, transforms, animation, audio, effects, events, and nested timelines need clear ownership so one track does not silently override another.

units.title: Cinematic workflow
units.content: Create shot hierarchy, establish camera and frame-rate policy, use sub-sequences by responsibility, lock approved timing, validate animation ownership, review game-state dependencies, and test final render path before long output.

units.title: Sequencer failure modes
units.content: Avoid deep nested overrides with unclear authority, mixing preview and final camera state, changing global timing late, and rendering before checking warm-up, streaming, and shot transitions.

drills.title: Structure a complex cinematic sequence
drills.prompt: Design a Sequencer organization for a multi-location music-video scene with animation, VFX, lighting, and shot revisions.

competencies.name: Performance, Memory & Streaming Diagnostics
competencies.description: Use Unreal profiling tools and runtime evidence to diagnose CPU, GPU, memory, shader, streaming, and hitch problems.
competencies.purpose: Optimize the measured bottleneck rather than guessing from editor feel.

units.title: Frame time is a pipeline of competing costs
units.content: Game thread, render thread, GPU, asset streaming, shader compilation, memory pressure, garbage collection, and async work can each dominate different frames.

units.title: Performance investigation loop
units.content: Capture target-platform traces, identify the dominant thread or subsystem, correlate hitches with loading and memory, isolate one cause, compare before/after traces, and preserve visual/gameplay acceptance criteria.

units.title: Optimization failure modes
units.content: Avoid optimizing editor traces as final truth, reducing quality globally before locating cost, hiding hitches with larger memory caches, and changing many scalability variables at once.

drills.title: Diagnose a traversal hitch
drills.prompt: Create a profiling plan for repeated hitches when entering a dense world partition area.

competencies.name: Build, Cook & Package Debugging
competencies.description: Diagnose build configuration, cooking, packaging, target-platform, plugin, asset-reference, and runtime-only failures.
competencies.purpose: Produce reproducible packaged builds and recover from release failures quickly.

units.title: Editor success does not prove packaged success
units.content: Cooking, asset discovery, plugin binaries, configuration, target platform, case sensitivity, and runtime permissions can differ materially from editor execution.

units.title: Packaging isolation workflow
units.content: Capture engine/project/plugin versions, reproduce from clean intermediates, separate compile from cook from stage/package from runtime failure, inspect logs, validate referenced assets, and compare with last known-good package.

units.title: Packaging failure modes
units.content: Avoid deleting all evidence before saving logs, changing plugins and engine versions during emergency debugging, relying on editor-only asset references, and overwriting the last working package.

drills.title: Diagnose a packaged-build failure
drills.prompt: Plan isolation for a project that runs in editor but fails after packaging.
